text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1% today to close at $131.83, extending a broader two-week decline. The immediate driver appears to be oil prices stabilizing rather than surging: after Saudi Arabia announced it would release additional crude supplies following a pipeline attack, crude concerns eased on September 17th, and oil finished flat on September 18th despite ongoing Middle East tensions. When supply disruption fears fade, energy stocks typically pull back even if geopolitical risk remains present.

The stock's weakness over the past week also reflects a broader pattern—the market is increasingly pricing in that Middle East conflict may not cause sustained oil shortages. Comments from Trump about nearing the end of the Iran war, combined with Saudi Arabia's willingness to offset pipeline losses with extra exports, have shifted trader expectations away from a tight supply picture. For an oil major like ConocoPhillips, that means lower odds of a significant rally from supply-driven price spikes.
